new-york-hudson-valley-rides-tarrytown-c.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: Food stop in North Stamford → High point near Sleepy Hollow is the logistics leg. Watch junctions, villages and speed changes, then let the roadbook do its job: move you out of the clutter without spending your best attention too early.

This High point near Sleepy Hollow → Scenic stretch in Parsippany stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

sections.to: Near Califon, on the way back
sections.advice: Scenic stretch in Parsippany → Near Califon, on the way back is the technical section. Hairpins, gradients and mixed traffic can stack up quickly; use low drama inputs, stay wide of centre lines and expect buses or riders appearing exactly where optimism says they will not.

sections.from: Near Califon, on the way back

sections.advice: Photo stop near Yorketown → Ridgefield can flow quickly, but only if you keep village limits and junction sightlines sacred. Fast connectors are where rides get untidy when fatigue creeps in.

safetyMarkers.note: Respect posted limits and assume enforcement near villages, viewpoints and main-road joins.

scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 65 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

scenicChapters.narrative: Speed drops and stays down. Park rather than crawl through. 55 km through ground somebody thought worth listing. The road passes it rather than bypassing it.

places-convent-of-la-encarnacion-hayedos.story: 383 km from Ávila to Ávila, about 6 h 36 of riding. It goes by way of Subsidiary building \La Casita del Infante, Old Town of Segovia and its Aqueduct, Hayedos de Ayllon - Montejo and back through Old Town of Segovia and its Aqueduct. The highest point is about 1,350 m. The line favours views over speed.
